name: The Count's Soiree
summary: Count Walzer holds a soiree, ostensibly to taste spice, truly to hear your violin — he wants to buy it.
narrative_beats: Candlelight, silver, warm voices. The Count pours your wine himself, but his talk circles the case in your arms.
'I have collected the finest instruments in the town,' he says, 'but never one that chooses its own listener. Name a price.'
The one in the case, languidly: "If you sell me to a noble with a carriage, I might carry you off — indirectly." He is waiting to hear how you answer.
player_options: Sell spice in bulk at a high price, never mention the violin (coins++, safe)
Let him hear a passage, raise your worth but don't sell (risky: he grows more fixed, may pull strings to check you)
Seriously consider selling the violin for the carriage and pass (a major choice: lose the spirit-companion for a shortcut out)
consequences: Sell spice: a big purse, enough for many legs of the road.
Sell the violin: never again that voice that punctures your self-deception and saves you money. The world goes quiet, and lonely — one ending of the the-vessel long game.
Dangle and refuse: the Count's fixation may turn into another danger — a man of wealth and power finds it easy to look into an out-of-town woman.
